overview: Two structures of the inner ear, one dedicated to hearing and the other to maintaining balance.
genZNote: Cochlea: the ear's sound-processing snail shell. Vestibular apparatus: the ear's built-in spirit level for balance.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Converts sound vibrations into nerve impulses for hearing.
aspects.valueB: Detects head position and movement, maintaining balance and equilibrium.

aspects.label: Structure
aspects.valueA: A coiled, snail-shaped tube containing the organ of Corti.
aspects.valueB: Consists of the semicircular canals, utricle, and saccule.

aspects.label: Associated Nerve Branch
aspects.valueA: Cochlear branch of the vestibulocochlear nerve (cranial nerve VIII).
aspects.valueB: Vestibular branch of the same vestibulocochlear nerve (cranial nerve VIII).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Both hearing and balance share the same cranial nerve (VIII, the vestibulocochlear nerve), just different branches — a commonly tested anatomical detail.
overlay.memoryTrick: Cochlea = hearing (co-CHLEA sounds like a shell for sound). Vestibular = balance.
overlay.commonMisconception: Balance problems don't always mean hearing is also affected, and vice versa — the two systems are anatomically close but functionally and neurally distinct.
